hypothesis: Adversarial multi-modal pre-training with dynamic semantic drift injection simulates long-horizon drift across text and vision to test factual consistency and contextual coherence over thousands of tokens without retraining or retrieval.
description: This method injects gradual, adversarially designed shifts in meaning within multimodal inputs during pretraining, mimicking how real-world usage accumulates ambiguity over time; by forcing the model to adapt internally to these evolving signals, it may learn more robust representations that resist coherence decay, potentially improving long-context reliability without additional compute at inference time

You will be given a research hypothesis in artificial intelligence, consisting of a Method, a Problem, and a Goal.
Rewrite it for a reader who is a researcher but not necessarily an AI specialist, in exactly this format:

Hypothesis: <ONE sentence of 20 to 30 words stating concretely what is done with the method, for which problem, to achieve which goal>
Description: <two or three sentences, 50 to 70 words in total, explaining the mechanism and why it could work>

Rules: the hypothesis sentence must have between 20 and 30 words: if the input is short, make it concrete by stating how the method would be applied; if the input is long, condense it to its core idea; begin the hypothesis sentence directly with the method (never with "This study", "This approach", "We", or similar); use plain, neutral language and at most one technical term per noun phrase; do not exaggerate; do not invent results, numbers, datasets, or citations; do not mention how the hypothesis was obtained; output only the two lines.

Method: Adversarial Multi-Modal Pre-Training with Dynamic Semantic Drift Injection
Problem: Generative AI models lose coherence and factual accuracy over extended interaction sessions due to unmodeled semantic drift in context windows
Goal: Achieve sustained factual consistency and contextual coherence across thousands of token generations without retraining or external retrieval
